so_what: nDabb is 7-0 on the league's best projected roster and ranks 13th of 14 at RB. Full PPR helps Puka Nacua most, now that Davante Adams' IR stint funnels Rams targets to him, and every catch counts a full point here. The league's best team has a hole at RB that it has every reason to trade for.

JayJBurn (5-2) holds Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who had 9 catches for 150 yards in Week 7 and now has six 100-yard games in seven. That is exactly the line full PPR rewards most. Javonte Williams' 155-yard Monday adds to it, and with Xavier Worthy still waiting on Rashee Rice's return, JayJBurn's only weakness is TE (11th).

kickkathsass (4-3) is the most exposed roster in the league, 14th of 14 in projected strength: Saquon Barkley played nine snaps Monday with a back injury, Rashid Shaheed's knee has no timeline, and Mike Evans and Rashee Rice both sat Week 7. Emanuel Wilson loses work once Charbonnet and Price are back. A thin team at 4-3 with full FAAB is a buyer.

chrisroraback (2-5) holds Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price together, so he keeps Seattle's backfield whichever back wins it, but Davante Adams (IR), Jaylen Waddle's Week 7 exit and Dallas Goedert in a slumping offense hit his pass catchers. Two straight weeks of injuries at 2-5 point to a seller.

sierragrace is 2-5 and holds Jalen Hurts, now expected out for the season, plus DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, who both sat Monday. Losing your QB at 2-5 in a 14-team league usually ends a season.

RBI11 (4-3) owns both Jahmyr Gibbs and Lamar Jackson and ranks last in projected WR points. Gibbs' ankle is reported minor and Jackson is reported likely back, and both are high-volume players whose value full PPR does not change. His need is WR, which full PPR pays more for than the other two leagues do, so he should be the most motivated WR buyer here.
No trades or claims have priced anything yet in this league: all fourteen owners still hold 100 FAAB, so the first real bid sets the market for the year.
